Interface ServerHttpRequest<B>

Type Parameters:
B - The body type
All Superinterfaces:
AttributeHolder, HttpMessage<B>, HttpRequest<B>, MutableAttributeHolder
All Known Subinterfaces:
FormCapableHttpRequest<B>
All Known Implementing Classes:
NettyHttpRequest, RawHttpRequestWrapper
public interface ServerHttpRequest<B> extends HttpRequest<B>
This interface extends HttpRequest with methods that are specific to a request received by an HTTP server.

  • Method Details

    • byteBody

      ByteBody byteBody()
      Get the bytes of the body. The body is owned by the request, so the caller should generally not close it or do any primary operations. The body is usually consumed by the argument binder of the controller, e.g. if it has a @Body argument. If you want to use the body, ByteBody.split(ByteBody.SplitBackpressureMode) it first.
      Returns:
      The body bytes of this request

    • whenResponseCompleted

      default boolean whenResponseCompleted(Consumer<@Nullable Throwable> callback)
      Run a callback once the response to this request is done: the final write of the response to the connection completed or failed, or the client went away before the response was written, also while the route has not answered yet. The failure is null if the response was written, else it is the error that the route failed with and that was answered with the default error response, the failure of writing the response, or a ConnectionClosedException if the client went away. The callback does not cancel or wait for the work of the route.

      The callback runs once. Unlike a listener of HttpRequestTerminatedEvent, it costs nothing for the requests that do not register one.

      Threading. The callback runs on the Netty event loop of the connection, directly after the final write completes, the client went away, or the request was cleaned up. If the response is done while the callback is being registered, it can run on the registering thread instead. The event loop also serves the other requests and connections assigned to it, so the callback must not block: no blocking IO (e.g. JDBC, blocking HTTP calls, file IO) and no long CPU-intensive work, which would delay every other connection of that event loop. Non-blocking work, e.g. completing a future, counting a metric or logging, is fine; hand anything else to an executor, e.g. the TaskExecutors.BLOCKING executor.

      Register before the response is handed to the connection, e.g. in the route, a filter before it continues, or a response filter: once the final write of the response was issued without a registration, its outcome cannot be told, and the registration is refused, even while that write is still in progress. For a WebSocket upgrade request that is upgraded, the response is done when the upgrade request is released, at the end of the session.

      Parameters:
      callback - The callback, given the failure of the response, if any
      Returns:
      false if the server does not support this, or the final write of the response was already issued, so the callback will not run
      Since:
      5.3.0

    • whenAbandoned

      default @Nullable Runnable whenAbandoned(Runnable callback)
      Run a callback when the client abandons this request before its response is written: the client closed the HTTP/1.1 connection, or reset the HTTP/2 stream of the request. This lets a route that answers asynchronously stop its work, e.g. cancel a pending CompletableFuture. The callback runs at most once. It is removed when the response is done.

      Threading. The callback runs on the Netty event loop of the connection, when the close of the connection or the reset of the stream is seen, or on the registering thread if the request was abandoned already. As for whenResponseCompleted(Consumer), it must not block the event loop: cancelling a future or setting a flag is fine; blocking IO or long CPU-intensive work belongs on an executor.

      Like whenResponseCompleted(Consumer), register before the response is handed to the connection: a callback registered after the final write was issued without a registration is refused, since it could not be kept while that write is in progress.

      Parameters:
      callback - The callback
      Returns:
      Removes the callback, or null if the server cannot tell when the client goes away, or the final write of the response was already issued
      Since:
      5.3.0
